prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1030; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection in Conroe, Texas, when the collision occurred. Driver 1 stated that the vehicle was turning left when Driver 2, traveling in the opposing lane, struck the front driver's side of the vehicle. Driver 2 gave a statement consistent with this account, and two independent witnesses at the scene described the sequence of events in the same way. Photographs taken at the scene show damage concentrated on the front left portion of Driver 1's vehicle, which is consistent with the reported impact. Officers observed no prior damage of a similar nature on the vehicle. A Passenger was also present in the vehicle at the time of the crash, and both officers and witnesses confirmed the Passenger's presence. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was transported to a local medical facility for evaluation. Officers noted that the reported injuries are plausible given the mechanism of this collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy associated with the vehicle.
